# Kern settings screen — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the Kern settings screen when settings need a page: the settings page block over section presets with sidebar or tab layout. `sections` are section-definition data — including the profile, security, preference, notification and auto-claim presets — so a whole settings page is one declaration, with row builders and the navigation adapter shared as one implementation each. `layout` picks sidebar for full pages and tabs for dialogs and narrow widths — never both, since there is one section list per screen — and active-section switching is the screen's only state, because rows own theirs. The canonical active-section trio keeps the painted and announced sections in agreement, with the sidebar layout pairing the navigation sidebar with a detail pane and the tabs layout rendering the dialog-tabs pattern.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the Kern settings screen when settings need a page: the settings page block over section presets — the native twin under the same contract, minus the layout choice. The native screen is always the grouped list: every section renders and section switching belongs to the host navigator, so there is no `layout` prop and no active-section value. `sections` are the preset section-definition data, so the whole page is one declaration rendered complete, `density` sets the row density across the screen's sections, and there is no per-row state on the screen — rows own theirs while the screen renders the data it is given.
